title: The Poker Game
cn: 第 5 集 · 扑克牌局
novel:
The weekend featured a poker game that turned into a battle of [[sides|side]]. Barney had to [[choose|choose]] between supporting Robin or his mother, Loretta, who had been [[arguing|argue]] with Robin all weekend.

Lily tried to [[coach|coach]] Barney on how to handle the situation. She advised him to be [[clever|clever]] and not pick a side directly. Instead, she suggested he use a [[strategy|strategy]] to make both women feel valued without offending either one.

Barney's attempts to stay neutral [[failed|fail]] when his mother [[demanded|demand]] that he take her side. Robin was equally [[stubborn|stubborn]] and refused to back down. The poker game became more [[tense|tense]] as the argument continued.

Meanwhile, Ted and Marshall had their own [[dispute|dispute]] over wedding gifts. They could not agree on who should give what. Marshall wanted to [[bet|bet]] on the outcome, but Ted thought it was a terrible idea. They [[competed|compete]] to see who could find the better gift.

In the end, Barney [[compromised|compromise]] by telling both Robin and his mother that he loved them equally. This [[satisfied|satisfy]] neither of them completely, but it kept the peace for the moment. Lily was proud of his [[diplomatic|diplomatic]] approach.

The poker game finally ended with Marshall winning the most chips. Ted [[admitted|admit]] that Marshall had found the better gift after all. The group laughed and enjoyed the rest of the evening together, [[relieved|relieve]] that the arguments were temporarily over.

side.en: She took her friend's side in the argument.

choose.en: He chose the red shirt over the blue one.

argue.en: They argued about money all night.

coach.en: She coached the team to victory.

clever.en: He found a clever solution to the problem.

strategy.en: They needed a new strategy for the game.

fail.en: She failed the driving test twice.

demand.en: He demanded an explanation from his boss.

stubborn.en: The stubborn child refused to eat.

tense.en: The atmosphere was tense before the announcement.

bet.en: He bet ten dollars on the game.

compete.en: The two companies competed for customers.
